The one document that says where the service is heading and whether it is getting there. Five sections, each changing at its own pace. It is a guiding document, not a plan: read top to bottom, it connects this year's direction to this sprint's work.

- **Definition:** [Glossary: Roadmap](/system/glossary)
- **Published:** quarterly, after quarterly planning. The sprint report section updates every sprint.
- **Owner:** product manager
- **Links to:** [Goal](/templates/goal), [Initiative](/templates/initiative), [Solution](/templates/solution), [Deliverable](/templates/deliverable), [Sprint report](/templates/sprint-report)

| Section | Changes | How it works |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Vision and strategy | Yearly | [03 Vision and strategy](/system/vision-and-strategy) |
| 2. Goals and goal progress | Goals yearly, progress quarterly | [04 Goals and goal progress](/system/goals-and-goal-progress) |
| 3. Now, Next, Later grid | Quarterly | [05 Now, Next, Later grid](/system/now-next-later-grid) |
| 4. Quarterly commitments | Set quarterly, status each sprint | [06 Quarterly planning and commitments](/system/quarterly-planning-and-commitments) |
| 5. Sprint report | Each sprint | [07 Sprint report](/system/sprint-report) |

You never fill the whole roadmap at once. Fill sections 1 and 2 at the yearly direction review, 3 and 4 at quarterly planning, and 5 every sprint. Each section's how-to is in the doc linked above.

## Template

### 1. Vision and strategy

| Field | What goes here |
|---|---|
| Vision (5+ years) | One or two sentences. A human outcome with no metrics or technology names, specific to this digital service. |
| Diagnosis | What is broken and why. Root causes, where the service is designed around government needs, and which constraints are real. |
| Guiding principles | Two or three decision rules: "When choosing between..., we'll prioritize..." |
| Focus areas | The journeys and problem types that get concentrated attention. |
| Key actions | 3-5 coherent moves across technology, staff, process and politics, each with one line on how it supports the others. |
| Tradeoffs | "We will not..." statements: what we defer, ignore or refuse in order to stay focused. |
| Reviewed | Date of the last direction review, who approved it, and the next review date. |

### 2. Goals and goal progress

One row per goal, updated at quarterly planning. The full goal statement, measure and source live in each [Goal](/templates/goal) artifact, not here.

| Goal | Started | Last | Current | Target | Progress |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Short name, linked to its Goal artifact | Baseline value | Last quarter's value | This quarter's value | Target value | Grey (no data yet), Green (on pace), Yellow (behind) or Red (moving the wrong way), judged against intended progress. Write the word too, not just the color |

### 3. Now, Next, Later grid

`Updated: [date]. Next update: [next quarterly planning]. Team: [people and roles this grid assumes].`

| Lane | Capacity | Now (this quarter) | Next (following two quarters) | Later (beyond) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Goal 1: [short name] | Strategic [50%], shared by all goal lanes | [Deliverable]: [concrete output] (of [Solution], [Initiative]) | [Solution]: will enable [user group] to [do something] ([T-shirt size]) (of [Initiative]) | [Initiative]: [problem or question, in users' terms] |
| Goal 2: [short name] | | | | |
| Goal 3: [short name] | | | | |
| Technical maintenance | [25%] | Whole row: [service levels]; [large planned maintenance, if any] | | |
| Small requests | [25%] | Whole row: [response-time commitment] | | |

Start mandated items with `Required:`. A Required item may have no Initiative: it traces to its mandate instead. Leave a cell empty when nothing fits.

### 4. Quarterly commitments

#### Planning overview

| Field | What goes here |
|---|---|
| Planning week | The four session dates |
| Quarter dates | First and last day |
| Working days | Weekdays minus holidays |
| Sprints | Count and dates |
| Hands-on team | People counted in capacity |
| Capacity split | Each work type as a percent, in days per person, and in sprints. If it differs from 50/25/25, say why |

#### Intended progress card (one per goal)

| Field | What goes here |
|---|---|
| Goal | Short name from the goal progress table |
| Intended progress | Milestone name, plus what we will be able to show by quarter end, with a number |
| Initiative | The active Initiative this goal's work belongs to |
| Deliverables | The commitment. Each one: name, parent Solution, delivery type (Release, In service, Hand off), size, status and target date |
| Dependencies | What a Deliverable needs from outside the team, or from discovery, with dates |

**Ongoing commitments**: one line each for Technical maintenance and Small requests, written as a service level.

**Planning notes**: days off, dependencies with dates, risks.

### 5. Sprint report

Updated every sprint. Uses the [Sprint report](/templates/sprint-report) template: sprint goal, stories committed and completed, unplanned work, status for each commitment grouped by Initiative and Solution, ongoing commitments, notes and sprint history.

## DMV example

The DMV roadmap for Q1, as it reads after the Sprint 3 review on Feb 14.

### 1. Vision and strategy

| Field | Entry |
|---|---|
| Vision | Oregon residents handle every vehicle and licensing need from any device, at the moment life calls for it, and finish feeling capable rather than processed. An office visit happens only for services that truly require one, and it means time with an expert who can help. |
| Diagnosis | The DMV is designed around government operational needs, not user outcomes. People need "vehicle and identity authorization," but what they experience is "navigate bureaucratic transactions." Multiple trips happen because our systems can't verify eligibility in real time, so we make people bring documents and hope. Counter staff spend their days processing routine transactions that a person could finish alone. |
| Guiding principles | When choosing between competing initiatives, we'll prioritize complete user outcomes over individual transaction efficiency. Our approach to balancing compliance and user experience will be real-time eligibility verification that ends "bring documents and hope" experiences. |
| Focus areas | Life event moments (getting a first license, buying a car, moving to Oregon) get concentrated attention. We'll actively investigate transaction completion barriers and staff workflow inefficiencies. |
| Key actions | 1. **Move vehicle registration renewal fully online, end to end.** This is our highest-volume transaction and the first proof that a resident can finish without a visit (Initiative: Online vehicle renewal). <br>2. **Build identity verification once and share it.** Every service that needs eligibility checks uses the same one, so real-time verification is built once (Initiative: Real-time eligibility verification). <br>3. **Redesign staff workflows alongside every release.** Counter staff are trained to take on complex cases as routine work moves online, which frees up the time that action 1 creates (Initiative: Counter staff on complex cases). <br>4. **Take on the first-license journey as one experience.** Applicants know they're ready before they arrive. This tests the life-event focus and depends on action 2. No Initiative yet; first-license questions sit in Later. |
| Tradeoffs | We will not digitize existing broken processes or optimize individual transactions in isolation. We will not pursue technology solutions without staff workflow redesign. We will defer back-office reporting upgrades unless they change a resident's or counter worker's experience. |
| Reviewed | November direction review. Approved by the executive steering group. Next review the following November. |

Q1 planning update. Full goal statements are in the [Goal](/templates/goal) example and the goals document.

| Goal | Started | Last | Current | Target | Progress |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 75% of renewals online within 5 minutes | 0% | 0% | 0% | 75% | Grey: no data yet |
| Zero multi-trip experiences for standard licenses | 85% | 85% | 85% | 0% | Grey: no data yet |
| 30% staff satisfaction improvement | Baseline | +2% | +5% | +30% | Green: on pace |

### 3. Now, Next, Later grid

`Updated: December 12. Next update: Q2 planning, March. Team: three developers, a UX designer and researcher, a content strategist, plus product manager, product owner, scrum master and technical architect.`

| Lane | Capacity | Now (this quarter) | Next (following two quarters) | Later (beyond) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Goal 1: 75% of renewals online within 5 minutes | Strategic 60%, shared by all goal lanes | Backend Integration and User Interface (of Vehicle Renewal Service, Online vehicle renewal) | Vehicle Renewal Service, next slices: open renewal to all eligible owners (XL) (of Online vehicle renewal) | Insurance verification delays: why do they frustrate people renewing? Online abandonment: why do people start online applications and not finish? |
| Goal 2: Zero multi-trip experiences for standard licenses | | Digital Identity Verification System (of Shared identity verification, Real-time eligibility verification). **Required:** update the donor check to comply with the new law | Shared identity verification, next slices: license eligibility rules (L) (of Real-time eligibility verification) | Complex transactions: what causes multiple trips for title transfers and moving to Oregon? |
| Goal 3: 30% staff satisfaction improvement | | Staff Training Program (of Staff workflow redesign, Counter staff on complex cases) | | |
| Technical maintenance | 20% | Whole row: security patches within 48 hours, uptime above 99.5%, legacy system support. **Required:** accessibility audit compliance | | |
| Small requests | 20% | Whole row: 2-week average response time for editor support, quick fixes and usability improvements | | |

Q1 runs 60/20/20 instead of the 50/25/25 default. Online renewal has a fixed public launch in Q2, and the team cleared its maintenance backlog in Q4, so Strategic gets the extra share this quarter.

### 4. Quarterly commitments

#### Planning overview

| Field | Q1 |
|---|---|
| Planning week | Dec 9-12 |
| Quarter dates | Jan 6 to Mar 31 |
| Working days | 59 (61 weekdays, minus two holidays) |
| Sprints | 6 two-week sprints, Jan 6 to Mar 28. Quarter review Mar 31. |
| Hands-on team | 5: three developers, a UX designer and researcher, a content strategist |
| Capacity split | 60/20/20, changed from the 50/25/25 default for the Q2 renewal launch |
| Strategic 60% | 35 days per person, 3.5 sprints, before organization business comes off the top |
| Technical maintenance 20% | 12 days per person, 1.2 sprints |
| Small requests 20% | 12 days per person, 1.2 sprints |

Fit check: the largest item, User Interface (L, 3-4 sprints), fits inside 3.5 Strategic sprints, but its date depends on legal approval of the payment gateway. That's why it carries the main risk.

#### Goal: 75% of renewals online within 5 minutes
- Intended progress: **Service ready.** Online renewal working, with 25 beta users completing renewals end to end.
- Initiative: Online vehicle renewal.
- Deliverables: Backend Integration, of Vehicle Renewal Service (Release, M, On track): in production by Feb 28. User Interface, of Vehicle Renewal Service (Release, L, On track): live for 25 beta users by Mar 28, with plain-language help text and confirmation page content by Feb 28.
- Dependencies: usability test findings from discovery by Feb 4. Payment gateway legal approval by Feb 21.

#### Goal: Zero multi-trip experiences for standard licenses
- Intended progress: **Infrastructure proven.** Digital identity verification at 99% uptime in production with real DMV data.
- Initiative: Real-time eligibility verification.
- Deliverables: Digital Identity Verification System, of Shared identity verification (In service, M, Committed): in service and tested with production data by Mar 28; work starts Sprint 4. Required: donor check update to comply with the new law (Release, S): live by Jan 31.
- Dependencies: security architecture review in week 2 of Sprint 4.

#### Goal: 30% staff satisfaction improvement
- Intended progress: **Staff ready.** 10 frontline staff can show they're able to guide residents through the new online process.
- Initiative: Counter staff on complex cases.
- Deliverables: Staff Training Program, of Staff workflow redesign (Hand off, S, Off track): training materials and sessions so 10 frontline staff are ready by Mar 28. Materials wait on the finished service and may push to early Q2.
- Dependencies: two workflow sessions with counter staff by Jan 24. The finished renewal service.

#### Ongoing commitments
- Technical maintenance: security patches within 48 hours, system uptime above 99.5%, legacy system support as needed.
- Small requests: 2-week average response time. Specific items come from weekly triage.

#### Planning notes
- Days off: Martin Luther King Jr. Day (Jan 20), Presidents Day (Feb 17), spring break coverage (Mar 10-14).
- Dependencies: legal approval of the identity verification process (in progress); legal approval of the payment gateway (Feb 21); security architecture review (Sprint 4).
- Risks: the staff training timeline assumes no major system issues during rollout. If legal approval slips, the User Interface slips with it.
